newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Regional currency pacts not enough - Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Regional currency pacts not enough - Mahathir.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday the agreements between central banks in Southeast Asia were insufficient to deal with the currency crisis facing the region.

"We already have some cooperation and arrangements. Obviously it is not sufficient or effective enough to deal with the kind of situation we are facing now," he said at the opening of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) foreign ministers meeting.
Mahathir did not spell out how the monetary authorities might boost their cooperation.

Asked if he was satisfied with the coordination of central banks in the region to defend their currencies, Mahathir told reporters after the speech, "Actually it could be improved ... everything can be improved."
Asian currencies came under renewed pressure again on Thursday with the Thai baht falling to a record low, leading the regional currencies a little further in their downward spiral.
Other neighbouring countries have also seen attacks on their currencies in the past month, forcing devaluations in Thailand and the Philippines and expensive intervention efforts in Malaysia.
In the past few years, central banks of the region and the Bank of Japan have struck repurchase pacts under which they would help each other defend their currencies if asked.
On Thursday, regional currencies dropped to new lows as speculators and corporates continued to pile into the dollar, triggering stop-loss orders.
